Razorpay gets licence to operate from GIFT City peerzada abrar Bengaluru, 2 November Razorpay, the omnichannel payments platform for busi- nesses in India, has received a ﬁnal Payment Service Provider (PSP) licence from the Interna- tional Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) to operate from GIFT City. The licence allows the company to move money into and out of India from GIFT City under a single regulatory framework. It follows the in- principle approval Razorpay received in April 2026, mark- ing another regulatory mile- stone for the company as it seeks to enable compliant cross-border ﬁnancial ﬂows to and from India. Rahul Kothari, chief oper- ations officer, Razorpay, said the company already facili- tates cross-border payments on both sides: Indian con- sumers paying global busi- nesses and Indian businesses collecting payments from cus- tomers around the world. “This licence adds a new dimension to that portfolio. It lets us move money in foreign currency, hold it in multi-cur- rency accounts, and serve ﬂows the domestic framework could not: from Indians invest- ing globally to NRIs looking after their families at home,” said Kothari. “As India’s ties with the world deepen, cross- border infrastructure must be as compliant and seamless as domestic payments. That is what we are aiming to build from GIFT City,” he added.
